title: Retraction
description: One row of llm-wiki/states/retractions.jsonl — an undo (retract) or redo (restore) of a run, replayed by load_state alongside the ledgers it governs (spec.md `### Ledger rows`, `### Replay`). retraction_id = rtr_ + 12 hex of sha256(target_run_id · action · timestamp); target_run_id names the run being retracted or restored, and run_id is the id minted for this undo/redo run itself (present on the matching states/audit_log.jsonl row too, never on the target's own rows, which are never rewritten). Folding retractions.jsonl in ledger order and keeping the last action per target_run_id is what a row proves: a target whose last action is retract is skipped on replay, one whose last action is restore is folded again.

retraction_id.description: rtr_ + 12 hex of sha256(target_run_id · action · timestamp). Content-derived, so parallel sessions never collide.

target_run_id.description: The run being retracted or restored.

by.description: The human who ran undo or redo — every reversal is audited as a human, never as the actor of the original run.

run_id.description: The id minted for this undo/redo run itself, distinct from target_run_id — the run that appended this very row.
